description: The eight relations charts driven by real PromQL against a live Prometheus/Mimir, scoped by cluster / namespace / client / server variables. Uses the instant table + label_join + organize + rowsToFields route, because the legendFormat + joinByField route only works for TestData: joinByField renames a Value field to its frame name, and a real Prometheus range query leaves frame.name unset, so every edge is dropped in silence.

options.content:
# Relations charts from a live Prometheus

The sibling of **ECharts Relations — Prometheus & Loki sources**, which feeds the same
eight charts from TestData. Everything here is real PromQL against `$prom`, scoped by the
variables in the top bar and bounded by `$topk`.

The two dashboards do **not** share a transformation chain, and that is the point.

### The TestData route does not survive the swap

`joinByField` widens N per-series frames by renaming each `Value` field to its **frame
name**. TestData's `predictable_csv_wave` sets one (`"name": "frontend-->gateway"`).
A real Prometheus range query with `Legend: {{client}}-->{{server}}` does not — the
rendered legend goes to `field.config.displayNameFromDS` and the frame name stays
unset. So the join yields a wide frame whose value fields are all still named `Value`.

`graphWide.endpointsOf()` reads `field.name` and `field.labels`, deliberately not
`getFieldDisplayName`. `"Value"` holds no `-->` and carries `client`/`server` rather
than `source`/`target`, so **every edge is dropped without an error**. Point live
queries at the TestData chain and you get the fixture's topology back, looking fine.

### This dashboard puts the identity in a column instead

`Format: Table` + `Type: Instant` gives one row per series; `label_join` builds the
`id`; `rowsToFields` turns each row into a field named by its `id`. No display-name
resolution anywhere in the path. The whole chain is two transformations:

| step | why |
| --- | --- |
| `organize` | `excludeByName` drops `Time` and the raw label columns, which would otherwise become stray labels; `indexByName` puts `id` first, because `rowsToFields` takes the first *string* column as the mark name and Prometheus sorts columns by label name; `renameByName` fixes `Value #A`/`Value #B` and the carrier labels |
| `rowsToFields` | no options needed — `id` → `field.name`, `Value` → the value, leftover strings → labels |

`organize` **is** `filterFieldsByName` + order + rename composed, so a separate
`filterFieldsByName` adds nothing. `renameByRegex` is worse than nothing here: it only
sets `config.displayName` and leaves `field.name` untouched.

Node-stat queries are bounded with `and on (server) …topk(…)`: a node field for a
service no edge reaches renders as a disconnected dot.

### One trap worth knowing

**A query must not name its columns `source` and `target`.** The plugin registers
`legacyToWide` as a panel transformation, and those run *upstream* of the dashboard's:

    SceneQueryRunner → PanelPluginDataTransformer → SceneDataTransformer (user)

Its trigger is exactly "has a `source` field and a `target` field", so an instant table
with those two column names gets claimed as the legacy row format and widened before the
chain above runs — the panel then shows **No data**, with nothing logged. Panels 4 and 8
below emit `src`/`dst` and let `organize` rename them.

### The variables

All of them are multi-select with `All` = `.*`, so every matcher in every query is `=~`,
never `=`. Prometheus interpolates a multi variable as a regex group — `(a|b)` — even
when one option is selected, which is exactly why `=` would silently match nothing.

| variable | source | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$prom` | datasource picker, `prometheus` | committed pointing at `ops-cortex-dev` |
| `$cluster` | `label_values(traces_service_graph_request_total, client_k8s_cluster_name)` | |
| `$namespace` | `label_values(…{client_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster"}, client_k8s_namespace_name)` | chained on `$cluster` |
| `$client` | `label_values(…{cluster, namespace}, client)` | chained on both |
| `$server` | `label_values(…{cluster, namespace}, server)` | chained on both |
| `$connection` | `label_values(…, connection_type)` | `database`, `messaging_system`, `virtual_node` |
| `$topk` | custom | edge budget per panel |

The service graph carries cluster and namespace **twice**, once per end
(`client_k8s_*` and `server_k8s_*`), so which end a panel filters on is a real choice:

- the dependency maps (1, 4, 8) scope the **client** side — "traffic originating in this
  selection, wherever it goes";
- the chords (3, 7) scope **both** ends, which is what keeps the matrix square;
- the cluster → namespace → service sankey (6) scopes the **server** side, since that is
  the hierarchy it draws.

`$client`/`$server` do not apply to the Kafka graph, where both ends are already pinned.

One consequence worth knowing: the service-graph processor emits **virtual nodes** for
external dependencies — `kafka`, `mysql` and friends come back with
`connection_type="virtual_node"` and **no** `server_k8s_*` labels at all. So any panel
scoped on the server side (6) excludes them by construction, and selecting one as
`$server` empties that panel while the client-scoped panels still draw it. That is the
data being honest, not a broken panel.

panels.description: Top-$topk service-to-service edges from Tempo's service graph, nodes coloured by error ratio. Scoped on the client side by $cluster / $namespace / $client / $server. Nodes are bounded by `and on (server)` to the endpoints the top-$topk edges reach.

panels.title: The label carrier — graph
panels.description: Same edges as panel 1, but `id` is `client:server` with no separator and the endpoints come from `source`/`target` labels. The query emits `src`/`dst` because a query that emits `source` and `target` is claimed by the plugin's legacy row-format pre-pass and renders No data.

options.content:
### 5 · Kafka fan-in / fan-out — graph (below left)

One query, `or`-joined: everything writing to `kafka`, and everything `kafka` writes to.
`$client`/`$server` do not apply — both ends are already pinned.

```promql
label_join(
  topk($topk,
    sum by (client, server) (
      rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{server="kafka", client_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",
        client_k8s_namespace_name=~"$namespace", client!=""}[$__range])
    )
  ),
  "id", "-->", "client", "server"
)
  or
label_join(
  topk($topk,
    sum by (client, server) (
      rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client="kafka", server_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",
        server_k8s_namespace_name=~"$namespace", server!=""}[$__range])
    )
  ),
  "id", "-->", "client", "server"
)
```

### 6 · Traffic by cluster → namespace → service — sankey (below right)

Three levels off one metric's server-side label set, `or`-joined into one query. The
levels must not share a name, or the sankey has a cycle.

```promql
label_join(
  topk($topk,
    sum by (server_k8s_cluster_name, server_k8s_namespace_name) (
      rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{server_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster", server_k8s_namespace_name=~"$namespace", server=~"$server", server_k8s_cluster_name!="", server_k8s_namespace_name!="", server!=""}[$__range])
    )
  ),
  "id", "-->", "server_k8s_cluster_name", "server_k8s_namespace_name"
)
  or
label_join(
  topk($topk,
    sum by (server_k8s_namespace_name, server) (
      rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{server_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster", server_k8s_namespace_name=~"$namespace", server=~"$server", server_k8s_cluster_name!="", server_k8s_namespace_name!="", server!=""}[$__range])
    )
  ),
  "id", "-->", "server_k8s_namespace_name", "server"
)
```

### 7 · Cross-cluster traffic matrix — chord

```promql
label_join(
  topk($topk,
    sum by (client_k8s_cluster_name, server_k8s_cluster_name) (
      rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster", server_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster", client_k8s_cluster_name!="", server_k8s_cluster_name!=""}[$__range])
    )
  ),
  "id", "-->", "client_k8s_cluster_name", "server_k8s_cluster_name"
)
```

### 8 · Parallel edges by `connection_type` — graph

One client/server pair, several connection types, filtered by `$connection`. The id takes
all three labels to stay unique, so it can no longer be split — the endpoints come from
the `src`/`dst` carrier. The `byRegexp` override dashes every `virtual_node` edge.

```promql
label_join(
  label_join(
    label_join(
      topk($topk,
        sum by (client, server, connection_type) (
          rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster", client_k8s_namespace_name=~"$namespace", client=~"$client", server=~"$server", client!="", server!="", connection_type=~"$connection",
            connection_type!=""}[$__range])
        )
      ),
      "id", " / ", "client", "server", "connection_type"
    ),
    "src", "", "client"
  ),
  "dst", "", "server"
)
```

panels.title: Kafka fan-in / fan-out — graph
panels.description: One `or`-joined query: {server="kafka"} is everything producing into Kafka, {client="kafka"} everything consuming from it. $client / $server do not apply — both ends are pinned.

panels.title: Traffic by cluster → namespace → service — sankey
panels.description: Three levels from one metric's server-side label set: server_k8s_cluster_name → server_k8s_namespace_name → server, `or`-joined. A sankey needs a DAG, so the three levels must not share a name. Because this one requires the server-side k8s labels, it excludes virtual nodes by construction — picking $server = an external dependency such as kafka empties it, which is the data being honest rather than a broken panel.

panels.title: Cross-cluster traffic matrix — chord
panels.description: client_k8s_cluster_name → server_k8s_cluster_name, both scoped by $cluster. Both labels are required non-empty: a series missing one would produce an id with an empty endpoint, which endpointsOf rejects.

panels.title: Parallel edges by connection_type — graph
panels.description: sum by (client, server, connection_type) gives several edges per pair, filtered by $connection. The id carries all three labels so it stays unique, which is exactly when the source/target label carrier is required.
